subject: ventures/mileage-deduction-method-calculator
professional: an enrolled agent / CPA who prepares Schedule C returns for self-employed drivers and checks Pub 463 chapter 4 first

evidence.correctness: Ran calc.mjs on the page's worked example (6000 H1 mi, 4000 H2 mi, 12000 total, $9,150 costs, $300 parking, 22% + SE). Recomputed by hand from the Pub 463 method (standard = miles x rate per period; actual = costs x business miles/total miles): standard 6000x0.725+4000x0.76 = $7,390.00 (tool 7390); business use 10000/12000 = 83.33%, actual 9150x0.8333 = $7,625.00 (tool 7625); parking +$300 to both; SE rate 0.153x0.9235 = 14.13%, taxRate 0.3613 (tool 0.3612955); break-even 7390/10000 = $0.739. All matched. Blocked-standard case forced 'actual'. Limit: irs.gov was unreachable from the sandbox (host not resolvable), so the 72.5c (Notice 2026-10) rate matches my own knowledge of the IRS notice but the 76c July 1 rate (Announcement 2026-11, after my knowledge) could only be cross-checked against the sibling mileage-log README, which the same author wrote. Arithmetic verified, the 76c figure not independently confirmed.
evidence.completeness: README/VENTURE/page claims checked: two half-year rates (works), actual-cost proration by business use (works), parking/tolls added to both (works), break-even cost per mile (works), rough tax value with optional SE tax (works), first-year-election lock-in warning (finding shown unless blocked), standard-rate-blocked toggle (works), business>total cap with warning (works), example loader/clear (in index.html, covered by page.test.mjs), disclaimer/usage opt-out (present), robots/sitemap/llms.txt (present). No stubs or TODOs found. VENTURE stage is 'prototype' and both hypotheses are untested.
evidence.verification: Ran node --test '*.test.mjs': 27 tests, 27 pass, 0 fail. Seeded three mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted afterwards (git status clean, 27/27 pass again): (1) changed the tie-break to standardTotal > actualTotal + 1000, caught (1 failure); (2) removed the Math.min(1,...) cap on business use, caught (1 failure); (3) second-half rate 0.76 -> 0.75, caught (6 failures). Gaps: no test for the 'tax savings on blocked standard' semantics or for tax-rate cap at 100; page tests are regex checks on HTML text, not DOM behaviour.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. Pure function, input sanitising via num() (NaN/negative to 0), no NaN output tested, clear comments with sources. Defects: findings are built as HTML strings and injected via innerHTML (values are numbers/constants so no XSS today); when standardBlocked is true, taxSavingsGap and gap are still computed against the unavailable standard figure; 'best' is silently 'actual' when blocked even if no actual costs were entered (shows $0 actual); rates hard-coded to 2026 with no year selector, so the tool goes stale each January.
evidence.claims: Checked: 72.5c/76c rates and dates (README, calc.mjs header, FAQ JSON-LD, page; 72.5c matches the IRS notice, 76c repeated consistently but not independently confirmable here); ineligibility rules (five or more cars, MACRS/179) match Pub 463 as I know it; 'nothing uploaded' (no network calls in calc.mjs; usage.mjs records counts only per its tests); disclaimer text asserted by page.test.mjs. Minor: llms.txt links the old github.io address rather than marisstella.app; README 'Figures (verified 2026-09-29)' is the author's own verification claim.
evidence.fitness: Walked a self-employed driver's job: enter H1/H2 business miles, total miles, car costs, parking, tax rate, get larger deduction, gap, tax value and the lock-in warning. Usable end to end and the half-year split is the real 2026 differentiator. A user with a lease or with only combined-year miles has to estimate the split by hand; no year-end annualisation of costs and no per-vehicle fleet handling.
evidence.domain: Compared against Pub 463 ch. 4 and Topic 510 practice. Core method right. Departures a preparer would flag: (a) no lease rule (standard rate must be used for the whole lease period including renewals; the tool only says 'a car you own'); (b) the blocked toggle lumps fleet, prior actual and MACRS/179 together and gives no guidance on a prior-year actual-then-switch case; (c) depreciation is user-typed, so the actual side is only as good as the user's number, and first-year MACRS vs straight-line is not modelled (stated limit); (d) tax value ignores the deduction for half of SE tax and the SS wage base (stated limit); (e) the standard-mileage depreciation component and its basis reduction are mentioned but not quantified; (f) the date-based split relies on the user's own mileage log, which is mentioned.

defects.what: Lease rule omitted: standard mileage rate must be elected for the full lease period; page only discusses owned cars, so a lessee could wrongly think they can switch later
76c July-1 rate and Announcement 2026-11 could not be verified against irs.gov by this audit; the only corroboration is the same author's mileage-log README
When the standard rate is blocked, the gap and tax-value rows still price the unavailable standard method; best is 'actual' even with no actual costs entered
llms.txt points at the old github.io address, not marisstella.app
Page tests are HTML regexes; no test runs the DOM handler or covers the blocked-case gap semantics

verdict: A small, correct, honest calculator. Its arithmetic matched a hand recomputation of the Pub 463 method on five outputs, the 27 tests pass, and three seeded mutations (tie-break, business-use cap, second-half rate) were each caught and reverted. It is finished against what it claims (stage prototype, untested hypotheses). The weaknesses are domain edges a tax preparer would raise first (no lease rule, blocked-case lumping) and one fact I could not verify independently because irs.gov was unreachable: the 76 cent July rate. It meets the bar on correctness, claims and verification with a median of 3; domain is the weakest dimension at 2.
